###Strategy

Let's use the table to think about the difference between how many books Kenji and Cameron each have. That will help us write an equation we can use to find how many books Cameron has when we know how many books Kenji has.

###Difference and equation

Month | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$
:- | -: | -: | -: | -:
Kenji | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$
 | $\maroonE{\downarrow+11}$ | $\maroonE{\downarrow+11}$ | $\maroonE{\downarrow+11}$ | $\maroonE{\downarrow+11}$
Cameron | $12$ | $13$ | $14$ | $15$

Cameron always has $11$ more books than Kenji, so we can write an equation to find how many books Cameron has in terms of how many books Kenji has:

$c=k+11$

question.content:
Cameron collects old books, and they convinced their friend Kenji to start collecting as well. Every month, they go to the store together, and they each buy a book. This table shows how many books they each have:

Month | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$
:- | -: | -: | -: | -:
Kenji | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$
Cameron | $12$ | $13$ | $14$ | $15$

They both want an equation they can use to find how many books Cameron will have ($c$) when Kenji has $k$ books.

**Complete their equation.**
